subject: OBS Studio
title: OBS Studio Alternatives in 2026
description: Ten live streaming and production tools to try instead of OBS Studio, from browser studios to Windows switchers, with pricing and trade-offs.
intro: OBS Studio is free and open source software for video recording and live streaming that runs on Windows 10 and 11, macOS 13.0 or newer, and Linux. Its homepage describes scenes built from multiple sources such as window captures, browser windows, webcams and capture cards. This page looks at the live streaming side only: tools that replace or sit beside OBS when you want a friendlier interface, a browser-based studio, built-in multistreaming or a heavier production switcher. Our [streaming software ranking for gamers](/software/best-streaming-software-for-gamers) covers the same field by use case.
why_switch: OBS asks you to build scenes and sources yourself, and some streamers want a studio that is already assembled around alerts and overlays.
A browser-based studio such as StreamYard or Lightstream removes the local install and the encoding load on the streaming PC.
Multistreaming is built into tools like Meld Studio and Prism Live Studio, where OBS needs extra setup for several destinations.
Corporate and event teams may need a production switcher with multi-camera workflows, which is where vMix and Wirecast sit.
Mobile contribution from a phone is a separate job that an app like Larix Broadcaster handles directly.

picks.name: Streamlabs Desktop
picks.pricing: The Streamlabs pricing page states that the company takes zero cut of your donations; plans for Desktop could not be read in full.
picks.note: Streamlabs presents itself as a streaming platform for Twitch, YouTube and Facebook, with Streamlabs Desktop, alerts, overlays, tipping and merch under one account. You gain an integrated set of creator extras so you are not wiring separate services together. You give up the plain, no-account simplicity of OBS, and we could not read the Desktop plan details because the product page renders with JavaScript, so check what is paid before you commit.

sources.fact: Streamlabs describes itself as a streaming platform for Twitch, YouTube and Facebook, offering Streamlabs Desktop, alerts, overlays, tipping and merch.
The Streamlabs pricing page states that the company takes zero cut of your donations.

picks.name: Meld Studio
picks.pricing: Meld is free at $0 per month; Meld Pro is $17 per month or $200 billed annually.
picks.note: Meld Studio calls itself free streaming and recording software with multistreaming to every platform at once and 4K recording. Its Meld Spark tool covers interactive overlays and alerts. You gain multistreaming without extra plumbing and a gallery of free overlays. You give up the huge plugin culture around OBS. The paid tiers are $17 per month for Pro, or $200 billed annually, so check what the free level leaves out.

sources.fact: Meld Studio is free streaming and recording software with multistreaming to every platform at once and 4K recording.
Meld's pricing page lists a free plan at $0 per month and Meld Pro at $17 per month, or $200 billed annually.

picks.name: XSplit Broadcaster
picks.best_for: Windows streaming with a polished UI
picks.pricing: Broadcaster Free is $0; Premium is $14.99 per month or $59.99 per year, and a lifetime option is offered.
picks.note: XSplit Broadcaster is live streaming and recording software for games, podcasts and presentations, with scenes, sources and outputs in one workspace. It runs on Windows only. You gain a commercial product with a free tier and a Premium plan that adds higher-resolution output and commercial use. You give up Mac and Linux support and the open source license, which matters if you want to inspect or modify the code.

sources.fact: XSplit Broadcaster is live streaming and recording software for games, podcasts and presentations.
XSplit's pricing page says Premium adds higher-resolution output and commercial use.

picks.name: Prism Live Studio
picks.best_for: Free multistreaming plus a mobile app
picks.pricing: The desktop app is free; a Plus subscription is sold through the PRISM mobile app.
picks.note: PRISM Live Studio is free software for live streaming and recording with multi-platform streaming and video editing. It runs on Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and on Apple Silicon Macs with Monterey 12.3 or higher, and has a mobile app. You gain simultaneous streaming and extras like screen sharing and AvatarLive. You give up Linux and Intel Mac support, and Credits are sold only in the mobile app.

sources.fact: PRISM Live Studio is free live streaming and recording software that provides multi-platform streaming and video editing.
PRISM Live Studio runs on Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit) and on macOS (Apple Silicon), Monterey 12.3 or higher.

picks.name: Lightstream
picks.best_for: Cloud streaming without a powerful PC
picks.pricing: Free tier at $0 with a Lightstream logo; Premium is $12, or $9 per month billed annually.
picks.note: Lightstream runs in the browser and needs no downloads, which suits streamers on weaker machines or consoles using cloud capture. The free tier gives 720p, a 10 hour limit per stream and up to 3 scenes with a logo on your stream. Premium removes the logo and adds 1080p and 20 scenes. You gain no encoding on your own hardware. You give up local control and the deep customization of OBS.

sources.fact: Lightstream's free tier costs $0 and includes 720p streaming, a 10 hour limit per stream and up to 3 scenes, with a Lightstream logo on all streams.
The Premium plan costs $12, or $9 per month on an annual subscription, and removes the Lightstream logo and adds 1080p and 20 scenes.

picks.name: vMix
picks.pricing: vMix shows a purchase option from $50 per month on its homepage and offers a free 60-day trial.
picks.note: vMix is a live streaming and live production video mixer and switcher for Windows PCs. Switch to it when your stream looks more like a TV broadcast than a gaming session. You gain a production-oriented tool, and a 60-day trial lets you test it properly. You give up a free price tag, since the homepage shows purchase from $50 per month, and you give up anything other than Windows.

sources.fact: vMix is a live streaming and live production software video mixer and switcher for Windows.
The homepage offers a free 60-day trial download.

picks.name: Wirecast
picks.pricing: Studio from $34 per month billed yearly ($408 per year) or $59 month to month; Pro from $42 per month billed yearly.
picks.note: Wirecast is live video streaming and broadcast software for Mac and Windows with unlimited cameras, remote guests and multistreaming. It fits corporate and event streams where several people join a show. You gain both operating systems and a free trial that includes every feature. You give up OBS's zero price, as Studio starts at $34 per month billed yearly. It also lacks Linux support on the pages we opened.

sources.fact: Wirecast is live video streaming and broadcast software for Mac and Windows, with unlimited cameras, remote guests and multistreaming.
The pricing page lists Wirecast Studio from $34/mo billed yearly ($408/yr) or $59 month to month, and Pro from $42/mo billed yearly.

picks.name: Ecamm Live
picks.pricing: Two plans at $16 per month and $32 per month, billed as $192 and $384 once, with a 14-day trial.
picks.note: Ecamm Live is a live streaming and video production studio built for Mac, requiring macOS 11.2 or newer. Mac users who find OBS fiddly may prefer its approach. You gain a Mac-native studio and a 14-day trial with no credit card. You give up Windows and Linux entirely. The two plans are listed at $16 per month, billed as one payment of $192, and $32 per month, billed as one payment of $384.

sources.fact: Ecamm Live is described as a live streaming and video production studio built for Mac and requiring macOS 11.2 or newer.
The pricing page states the free trial lasts 14 days and does not require a credit card.

picks.name: StreamYard
picks.pricing: A free plan exists; the individual plan is $18.99 per month billed monthly, or $14.99 billed yearly.
picks.note: StreamYard is a browser-based live streaming and recording studio that streams to Facebook, YouTube and other platforms. It is a fit for talk shows and webinars where guests join from a link. You gain no install and a free plan with local recordings of 2 hours per month. You give up scene-level control and capture of games, so it is closer to a meeting-style studio than OBS.

sources.fact: StreamYard describes itself as a professional live streaming and recording studio in the browser that streams to Facebook, YouTube and other platforms.
The StreamYard pricing page lists an individual plan at $18.99 per month billed monthly, or $14.99 per month billed yearly (22% off), with a 7-day free trial.

picks.name: Larix Broadcaster
picks.note: Larix Broadcaster is a free mobile broadcasting app from Softvelum for remote contribution streaming from Android and iOS devices. It does not replace a desktop studio, but it covers the case where your camera is a phone in the field. You gain a free contribution tool. You give up scenes, overlays and any desktop production features, so most people would send its feed into another tool rather than use it alone.

sources.fact: Larix Broadcaster is free mobile broadcasting software for iOS and Android devices.
The page describes the apps as tools for remote contribution streaming from Android and iOS.

how_to_pick: Decide first where the stream is produced. A weak PC or a console points to Lightstream. A Mac points to Ecamm Live. Guests joining by link point to StreamYard. A Windows rig for a multi-camera show points to vMix, and a Mac or Windows one to Wirecast. If you want multistreaming without extra setup, try Meld Studio or Prism Live Studio first because both are free to start. Keep OBS installed while you trial, since its free license makes it a safe fallback if a trial falls short.

faqs.q: Why would anyone leave a free tool like OBS Studio?
faqs.a: Usually for workflow, not cost. OBS is free and open source, but you assemble scenes yourself. Browser studios, built-in multistreaming and production switchers each save time on a specific job. Some teams also want a vendor behind the software.

Meld Studio and Prism Live Studio are described as free, XSplit Broadcaster has a free tier at $0, and Lightstream has a free tier with a logo on your stream. Larix Broadcaster is free for mobile. Always read the limits of each free level.
OBS supports macOS 13.0 or newer. Ecamm Live is Mac-only, Wirecast runs on Mac and Windows, and Prism Live Studio supports Apple Silicon Macs. XSplit Broadcaster and vMix are Windows tools.
Yes. StreamYard and Lightstream both run in the browser, so nothing needs installing. That helps on locked-down computers, though you give up the local scene control that OBS gives you.

faqs.q: Can I keep using OBS next to these tools?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Some teams use OBS as the encoder and a cloud tool for distribution. Check each vendor's documentation for supported inputs before you rely on that setup for a live event.
